claims.text: The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy with dendritic/interdendritic micro-segregation that causes asymmetric XRD peaks.
The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has significantly low room-temperature fracture strain.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr induces precipitation of a C14 Laves phase in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
The Cr-induced C14 Laves phase has a volume fraction of approximately 4%.
The C14 Laves phase forms a reticulated, interconnected network localized in interdendritic regions.
A reticulated Laves-phase network forces cracks onto tortuous or deflected paths rather than permitting straight crack propagation.
Crack deflection by the reticulated Laves phase increases room-temperature fracture strain.
C14 Laves phases are brittle and can increase cracking tendency in BCC-based alloys.
Cr dissolved in the BCC matrix contracts its lattice parameter.
Contraction of the BCC lattice should produce an XRD peak shift toward higher 2θ.
Solute-associated lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion and produces solid-solution strengthening.
The strengthening caused by Cr-associated lattice distortion counteracts the embrittlement associated with the Laves phase.
Negative enthalpy of mixing between Cr and the Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr host elements drives the proposed lattice contraction.
A W-Ta-Cr-V model provides an analogous thermodynamic basis for the proposed Cr-driven behavior.
Homogenization at 1000-1200 °C can suppress amorphous formation while allowing C14 Laves-phase nucleation in the Cr-modified alloy.
Cooling can preserve the interdendritic segregation morphology after homogenization.
The beneficial response occurs only when the Cr concentration remains near 4 at.%.
Increasing Cr beyond approximately 4 at.% may create a continuous brittle Laves network that reduces fracture strain.
Exceeding the Cr solubility limit in the BCC phase may prevent sufficient lattice contraction.
The appearance of C14 Laves-phase diffraction peaks should accompany the improved fracture strain and BCC lattice contraction.

contradictions.description: The proposed homogenization treatment is intended to reduce chemical inhomogeneity, while the required mediator depends on preservation of interdendritic segregation; no processing logic is supplied to reconcile these competing objectives.
